claim_ceiling: This file is a case register and test-to-case traceability index. Rust unit tests listed here are synthetic reference tests, not independently adjudicated benchmark outcomes, vendor comparisons, SAWEM operator verification or investment-performance results. Cases marked not_run have no measured result. The DSU price-curve unit tests remain synthetic price-lookup conformance, not evidence of DSU product admission, reserve qualification, settlement or revenue. DSU qualifying-capacity tests cover only the named synthetic Code arithmetic branches; they do not authenticate source records, implement utilized-service alternatives, calculate performance-adjusted payments or establish market qualification. Reserve-capacity payment tests are exact formula checks over synthetic or prequalified inputs; they do not establish reserve-category prices, real qualifying capacity, operator performance factors, market admission, settlement or received cash. DSU capacity-path tests distinguish utilized, changed-instruction and unchanged-instruction cases and apply the effective-availability ceiling; acceptable-performance decisions are still supplied as prequalified inputs. The reserve payment formula rejects a reserve-category price labeled for a different reserve product. The constrained-schedule oracle integrates a synthetic piecewise-constant curve over signed schedule values with explicit Trading Period duration; it is not a Market Operator settlement reproduction and does not authenticate schedules, price submissions or market statements. The credit-cover increment computes only source-calendar-backed deadlines and notice timeliness; it does not calculate Actual Exposure, Undefined Potential Exposure, UEF, Required Credit Cover, collateral sufficiency or project liquidity. Credit-cover exposure arithmetic counts unpaid invoices and uninvoiced Settlement Statement amounts without double counting, but accepts Undefined Potential Exposure as an externally supplied value and does not calculate the Market Operator UEF or annual Required Credit Cover parameters. Remediation only counts receipt-backed early invoice payments and collateral posted by the explicit deadline; it does not model bank-provider creditworthiness or guarantee cash availability. Credit-cover remediation validates unique receipt references and source-digested civil-date coverage; it still does not authenticate the real bank/Market Operator source or model provider creditworthiness. Funding-option economics are simple-interest scenario calculations using externally supplied participant funding cost and Collateral Reserve Account yield. They compare only the two paths listed in §15.10.2(3); they do not prove bank or account eligibility, live availability of funds, actual interest credited, or optimal investment funding. Rev 2.3's acceptable Credit Cover form is a cash-held deposit in a Collateral Reserve Account; generic bank guarantees and letters of credit are not modeled as permitted alternatives. undefined The credit-cover amount calculation is a synthetic sum of exposure components and supplied UPE, not the MO's full §15.10.3 Actual Supplier Exposure / UEF result. New deadline coverage includes provider replacement within ten Business Days and advance notice of Posted Credit Cover changes one Business Day beforehand. Liquidity stress snapshots distinguish externally supplied MO Required Credit Cover and Posted Credit Cover from treasury cash headroom. Potentially fundable cover is not posted cover and assumes no transfer or MO acceptance until separately evidenced. The module does not calculate UEF, post collateral, predict cash availability, or infer the timing of payment-system transfer. The liquidity waterfall is a dated scenario projection with committed, forecast and adverse-stress paths. It does not authenticate forecast receipts, prove bank transferability/cash availability, increase Posted Credit Cover for planned deposits, or establish the Market Operator's Required Credit Cover beyond source-bound inputs. Forecast-vintage replay reconstructs only synthetic/prequalified records available by a frozen decision time. It is not a forecasting model, market price feed, source-authentication mechanism or evidence of improved forecast accuracy; rolling-origin calibration and live/historical backtests remain not_run. Forecast calibration scoring is an exact-accumulator implementation over synthetic/prequalified forecasts and realized observations. It does not establish feed authenticity, model calibration on real market data, predictive superiority, forecast value capture or comparative performance; rolling-origin, project/time holdout and vendor baselines remain not_run. Execution-fidelity metrics compare synthetic signed scheduled energy with synthetic meter/settlement records. They do not prove actual asset performance or calculate SAWEM imbalance settlement; the public M5BAT field dataset and a source-frozen replay remain to be acquired and independently reproduced. The BMS capability evaluator is a SOC-only, synthetic/ source-qualified curve interpreter. No M5BAT field curves have been fitted, and temperature, SOH, cell voltage, imbalance and dynamic BMS state are not modelled; operational qualification and power-delivery improvement are not demonstrated. The revenue-realization bridge is an evidence-attribution kernel tested on synthetic signed adjustments. It does not forecast prices, calculate SAWEM settlement, validate the completeness of source systems or establish that its category allocation is causally unique. Any unclassified/unobserved difference remains an explicit residual; no empirical realization factor or revenue improvement has been measured.

cases.title: Standalone BESS feasible discharge
cases.scenario: A synthetic BESS dispatches from an admissible initial SOC with transition downtime and reserve commitments inside its operating envelope.

cases.title: PV+BESS shared point-of-connection
cases.scenario: PV and BESS jointly use a capped point of connection; charging source and export allocation must reconcile by interval.

cases.title: SOC floor protection
cases.scenario: A discharge request would move stored energy below the minimum usable-energy boundary.

cases.title: SOC ceiling protection
cases.scenario: A charge request would move stored energy above the maximum usable-energy boundary.

cases.title: Energy and reserve power overlap
cases.scenario: Scheduled discharge plus upward reserve exceeds the declared continuous discharge rating.

cases.title: Insufficient operating-mode transition
cases.scenario: A dispatch requests a mode change before the registered directional transition time has elapsed.

cases.title: Daily energy declaration cap
cases.scenario: One or more daily declared energy values exceed the daily Trading Unit limit.

cases.title: Next-six-day and seven-day aggregate caps
cases.scenario: The six-day forward sum or seven-day total exceeds its own independent MWh limit.

cases.title: Network-constrained charging
cases.scenario: Charging is curtailed or rescheduled when the POC import constraint binds despite local surplus energy.

cases.title: Network-constrained discharge
cases.scenario: A discharge exceeds the POC export cap; the invalid candidate energy state must not be committed.

cases.title: Intra-day re-declaration gate
cases.scenario: A revised schedule arrives after the relevant market gate closure for the frozen rule version.

cases.title: Instruction-to-meter reconciliation
cases.scenario: Authenticated instructed and metered outcomes differ at a correctly identified Trading Period and boundary.

cases.title: Cumulative balancing components
cases.scenario: Multiple signed balancing-payment components are summed with checked arithmetic without collapsing their identities.

cases.title: Settlement statement rerun
cases.scenario: A later settlement statement revision changes a prior liability or cash-flow assumption and invalidates the earlier underwriting state.

cases.title: Credit-cover arithmetic and overflow
cases.scenario: Actual exposure plus undefined-potential exposure is reconciled using integer minor units and checked overflow.

cases.title: Warranty-envelope breach
cases.scenario: A high-revenue dispatch policy breaches a warranty operating envelope or excluded operating condition.

cases.title: Rare price spike and negative-price stress
cases.scenario: A forecast-informed policy is evaluated on an unseen price-spike or negative-price scenario without future information leakage.

cases.title: Forecast regime shift
cases.scenario: Forecast calibration degrades after a structural shift; confidence and policy must update without look-ahead.

cases.title: Forced outage invalidates declared capability
cases.scenario: A forced outage removes previously declared or certified availability and invalidates reserve and revenue assumptions.

cases.title: Rule supersession invalidates prior eligibility
cases.scenario: A new or superseding rule profile invalidates a prior product eligibility conclusion at its effective-time frontier.

cases.title: Upward reserve from reducing charging
cases.scenario: A charging BESS provides upward reserve by reducing net import before increasing discharge; the target remains physically admissible.

cases.title: Downward reserve from reducing discharge
cases.scenario: A discharging BESS provides downward reserve by reducing export and, if needed, increasing charging.

cases.title: Reserve setpoint in minimum-charge deadband
cases.scenario: The requested reserve activation leaves the asset at a charging setpoint below minimum stable charging power.

cases.title: Product-specific reserve response and sustain
cases.scenario: Regulating, instantaneous and ten-minute reserve use their own SAWEM response definitions; no unspecified sustain duration is invented.

cases.title: Missing sustain obligation remains indeterminate
cases.scenario: A product whose Code definition has no minimum sustain duration lacks a separate operator/contract sustain obligation and must remain indeterminate.

cases.title: Reserve response conflicts with mode-transition time
cases.scenario: Asset full-activation evidence is faster than its registered transition path, or the registered transition exceeds the product activation deadline.

cases.title: Contracted reserve capacity vs qualifying paid capacity
cases.scenario: A Trading Unit has contracted reserve MW but effective availability, SO performance adjustment, actual energy dispatch or response evidence limits its capacity qualifying for payment.
required_evidence: SO performance criteria and performance adjustment

cases.title: Product-specific reserve lost-opportunity pricing
cases.scenario: Four SAWEM reserve opportunity-price rules are evaluated against a synthetic generating incremental price curve; product-specific elbow selection, formula sign, MCR/Emergency Level 1 boundaries, unsupported directions and checked arithmetic are covered.

cases.title: Demand-side reserve price from descending consumption curve
cases.scenario: A Demand Side Unit uses the declared-consumption and three-elbow curve; contracted-consumption points at elbows select the next non-empty lower-consumption price block, while the third elbow has no remaining reducible block.
required_evidence: first, second and third consumption elbow points

cases.title: DSU product-specific qualifying capacity
cases.scenario: Demand-side Regulating Up and Instantaneous qualification distinguishes utilized reserve, non-utilized reserve with a changed energy instruction, and the ordinary non-utilized consumption-curve path; effective availability caps each branch, missing performance/instruction evidence remains indeterminate. Ten-Minute uses effective available capacity less the third elbow.
required_evidence: effective available capacity for the Trading Period
official energy consumption and declared consumption for the ordinary non-utilized path
whether a non-utilized unit received a different energy instruction
System Operator acceptable-performance assessment or explicit no-criteria state

cases.title: Product-specific reserve capacity payment arithmetic
cases.scenario: A reserve-category price from the Market Operator is multiplied by already-qualified contracted reserve MW and the correct product-specific performance adjustment; Ten-Minute excludes the adjustment, uncontracted reserve receives zero, and unresolved evidence remains indeterminate.
required_evidence: System Operator reserve-category price for exact Trading Period
System Operator performance adjustment factor where criteria are established
reserve-category price explicitly typed to the payment product

cases.title: Unconstrained-to-constrained schedule adjustment
cases.scenario: The Market Operator integrates the submitted stepwise incremental price curve over the exact signed-MWh-per-Trading-Period interval between the Unconstrained and Constrained Schedules; schedule increase is a payment and reduction is a charge. Explicit no-price-submission is R0/MWh; unknown source state and gaps in the curve remain indeterminate or invalid. The schedule is energy per Trading Period, not an inferred MW value.
required_evidence: exact Trading Unit and Trading Period
Unconstrained Schedule and Constrained Schedule revisions
authoritative day-ahead incremental price submission state
complete signed milli-MWh-per-Trading-Period incremental price curve covering the schedule-energy delta
price-curve segment units and source revision

cases.title: Daily credit-cover recalculation and posting deadline
cases.scenario: The kernel calculates the daily Business Day notice and separate second-Working-Day posting deadline; the two-Business-Day Credit Call re-establishment deadline; the ten-Business-Day qualifying-bank replacement deadline after provider cessation; and one-Business-Day advance notice before a Posted Credit Cover change. Separately, a synthetic exposure-component reconciliation sums issued-unpaid invoices and uninvoiced Settlement Statement balances with externally supplied UPE and evaluates receipt-backed remediation. It does not reproduce the MO's full §15.10.3 historical-activity / ASE / UEF calculation.

Undefined Potential Exposure amount and its model/UEF provenance receipt

increase notice civil date and timestamp

separate Working Day calendar, source digest and coverage horizon
early invoice payment receipts and additional collateral posting receipts

provider cessation / loss-of-eligibility date and effective status
replacement qualifying bank evidence and re-post receipt
advance notice to the Market Operator before a Posted Credit Cover change
provider cessation / loss-of-eligibility date and effective status
replacement qualifying bank evidence and re-post receipt
advance notice to the Market Operator before a Posted Credit Cover change

cases.title: Compare cash collateral carry against early-invoice payment
cases.scenario: For an equal Required Credit Cover relief amount, compare the simple-interest cost of a cash deposit in the Market Bank Collateral Reserve Account (participant funding cost less account interest, across an explicit lock-up horizon) with advancing an issued outstanding invoice (participant funding cost across the days advanced). Return cash use, restricted cash, invoice liability reduction and exact rational cost separately. Missing rates, provider/account/invoice evidence remain indeterminate; the model must not admit generic bank guarantees or letters of credit as an alternative under Rev 2.3.
required_evidence: source-referenced qualifying Credit Cover Provider bank eligibility
source-referenced Collateral Reserve Account establishment at the Market Bank
participant marginal funding/opportunity-cost rate and its source/version
actual Collateral Reserve Account interest rate and bank source/version
issued invoice identity, outstanding balance and issue-status evidence
invoice due date and early-payment date
funding fees and assumptions for the selected horizon

cases.title: Treasury cash-at-risk against externally determined Required Credit Cover
cases.scenario: Given source-referenced MO Required Credit Cover, Posted Credit Cover, unrestricted treasury cash, mandatory non-cover outflows and a separately approved operating cash floor, distinguish current cover shortfall from cash potentially available above the floor and any remaining external funding gap. Potentially fundable cash is not Posted Credit Cover until a separate posting receipt is evidenced. Missing MO cover remains indeterminate.
required_evidence: Market Operator Required Credit Cover amount and source receipt for the snapshot
Posted Credit Cover balance and source receipt
unrestricted treasury cash balance and source receipt
mandatory non-cover outflows due in the same horizon and source ledger
Board/treasury-approved minimum operating cash floor and its authority
civil-date calendar mapping the snapshot day ordinal
evidence references that prove the amount sources do not overlap or double count

cases.title: Event-ordered treasury cash waterfall through the cover deadline
cases.scenario: Replay dated committed receipts/obligations, forecast receipts/flows and adverse stress adjustments in strict timestamp/sequence order. Produce separate cash paths, minimum unrestricted cash, first operating-floor breach, cash headroom at the Credit Cover deadline, deadline cover shortfall and potential external funding gap. Credit Cover requirement may be reassessed as new MO source evidence arrives. Planned Collateral Reserve Account cash lock-up and early invoice payment reduce projected unrestricted cash but do not increase Posted Credit Cover; a separate receipt-backed posting record is required. A later downward reassessment must not erase the peak shortfall observed before the deadline; the deadline's own gap is reported separately. A deadline earlier than the evaluation start timestamp is invalid. Any event earlier than the projection start timestamp, including earlier on the same civil date, is rejected.
required_evidence: source-digested civil calendar covering the full cash projection horizon
opening unrestricted cash balance and source receipt
Board/treasury minimum operating cash floor and authority
committed receipts and mandatory outflows with source references and timestamps
forecast cashflows, forecast vintages and confidence/quality labels
adverse liquidity stress events and their scenario definitions
Market Operator Required Credit Cover notice and revisions with effective timestamps
current Posted Credit Cover and receipt evidence
Credit Cover Increase Notice deadline and timezone
planned collateral deposit and early invoice payment cash requirements
explicit IANA timezone for local event minute interpretation
unique source receipt references for each cash event
unique event source references to prevent duplicated cash movements

cases.title: Leakage-free as-of forecast vintage reconstruction
cases.scenario: For each price/forecast target period and model identity, reconstruct only the forecast vintages and realized observations that were available to the decision workflow at the frozen decision timestamp. Select the latest eligible forecast by issue time, let a realized observation supersede only after the target interval ended and the observation became available, exclude future-known records, report missing coverage, and reject ambiguous latest vintages. Forecast issue time, target valid time and source available-at time are separate. A target without a model identity must not silently choose among different forecasting engines; the caller must explicitly scope the target by model. Source availability is distinct from issue time: a forecast issued before decision time but published after the decision is excluded. A known realized observation is model-independent, so it may supersede competing forecast engines without requiring a model identity. Model scope is the pair of immutable model label and exact model SHA-256; builds sharing a label but not a digest are separate forecasting engines.
required_evidence: frozen historical decision timestamp in UTC
target Trading Period start and end timestamps
forecast model identity and executable/model content digest
forecast issue timestamp and source available-at timestamp
realized price observation valid-time and observation timestamp
source retrieval/publication timestamp and content digest
sealed project/time holdout membership and decision-time evidence frontier
separate source availability timestamp even when forecast issue time is earlier
model identity and digest for each competing forecast engine
known realized observation takes precedence only after target interval end and source availability
separate source available-at timestamp distinct from issue time
forecast model identity and digest for every forecast-engine vintage
realized observation interval end, observed-at and available-at timestamps
exact immutable forecast-model content digest bound to the decision target

cases.title: Leakage-free probabilistic forecast calibration and scoring
cases.scenario: For one exact immutable forecasting model build, score quantile predictions against realized Trading Period prices that were available by the evaluation timestamp. Forecasts must have been issued and available by each historical decision time and target a future valid interval. Compute median MAE, signed bias, squared-error sum, q10/q50/q90 pinball loss, empirical quantile coverage, central-80% interval coverage and exact weighted interval score. Quantile crossing, future-known forecast/actual data, mixed model builds and duplicate target periods are rejected.
required_evidence: frozen historical decision timestamp per forecast target
forecast issue and source availability timestamps
exact target Trading Period start/end interval
q10/q50/q90 forecast values and currency/unit declaration
forecast model identity and exact model SHA-256
realized market price, target interval and observed-at timestamp
realized source availability timestamp and content digest
sealed project/time holdout membership and cohort definition

cases.title: Evidence-bound schedule-to-meter execution fidelity
cases.scenario: Compare signed scheduled export/import energy against signed meter energy over a frozen horizon. Report schedule, meter and settlement time coverage separately; absolute deviation, unfulfilled scheduled energy and overdelivery; and fulfilment only when the full schedule horizon is covered by meter evidence. Reconcile actual booked balancing charges only when source-bound settlement evidence exists for every interval. Future-known meter/settlement records, duplicate record IDs, overlapping intervals and schedule revisions published after delivery start are rejected. Intervals must be ordered by start timestamp, then must not overlap. A schedule revision published after delivery start and a meter observation before the interval has ended are invalid; settlement evidence cannot exist without matching meter evidence.
required_evidence: frozen optimized/market schedule interval and schedule content digest
schedule issue timestamp and source availability timestamp no later than interval start
signed metered grid energy for the matching delivery interval
meter record identity, source content digest and observation/availability timestamps
settlement statement line item for actual balancing charge or credit
settlement evidence source digest and availability timestamp
explicit interval duration, timestamp timezone and sign convention
complete expected evaluation horizon and all interval records

cases.title: Evidence-qualified SOC-dependent charge/discharge capability envelope
cases.scenario: Evaluate requested charge or discharge power against separate source-bound piecewise-linear conservative capability curves over the declared SOC calibration range. Interpolation rounds down, SOC outside the calibration range is rejected rather than extrapolated, malformed/unsorted curves fail closed, and synthetic-only assumptions cannot claim a non-synthetic evidence basis and are never operational authorization. This is a bounded SOC-only envelope; temperature, SOH, cell voltage, imbalance and dynamic BMS state remain separate future dimensions.
required_evidence: battery-unit identity and rated AC-side power
source-digested conservative charge and discharge capability points
declared SOC calibration minimum and maximum
source evidence basis: field-measured conservative envelope, manufacturer guaranteed envelope or synthetic scenario
measurement campaign identity, test conditions and source availability
separate temperature/SOH/voltage/imbalance evidence before multi-dimensional use

cases.title: Evidence-attributed bridge from theoretical revenue to realized net cash
cases.scenario: Reconcile theoretical gross revenue to realized net cash using source-bound signed adjustments for forecast regret, availability, execution deviation, balancing settlement, market fees, degradation/warranty, financing/collateral and contract/curtailment effects. The caller declares which categories are required for the asset/contract. If any required category is absent, the bridge remains incomplete, only partial reconstructed net is reported, and the unexplained residual/realization ratio are withheld. Future-known evidence, invalid source hashes and duplicate component IDs are rejected. This decomposes effects that aggregate revenue realization haircuts combine. One source receipt cannot back two adjustment components under different component IDs.
required_evidence: theoretical gross revenue and exact model/input digest
realized net cash from bank and settlement receipts
forecast vintage and decision-time replay for forecast-regret component
booked balancing settlement statement line items
evaluation-as-of timestamp and source availability time for every component
unique source reference for each revenue adjustment component to prevent double-counting
